title: Millhaven Expanded - Twelve Lives
objective: Begin at 05:00 asleep in your own cottage. When your scheduled wake/work-start time arrives, leave home and walk to your workplace using actual go actions before optional errands; never start work before waking or travel by teleportation. Keep Millhaven alive as twelve independent villagers, each contributing useful work. Torvin makes and fits wagon parts, retrieves his shovel, and digs the well with Bren using actual shovel, timber and rope; helpers can carry supplies separately. Bren feeds the real horse at the stable, leads it to the wagon, hitches it for delivery, then unhitches and returns it at night. Nella accepts the six-unit road-only supply circuit; Ada or Jory may substitute when she is busy. Bread should reach the tavern by day-one 19:00; an overdue warning allows late recovery. Rowan accepts the timber foot route to Hobb's workshop. After the mill fails at 14:00, Hobb brings beam, hammer and one actual plank to the watermill; Hobb and Mara each contribute repairs. Confirm meetings, share known routes, and read public stock and project reports. Process two production inputs per action, including cooking fish; replenish hay, herbs, logs and paid noon trader iron. Use manure for faster harvests and tea for tiredness relief. Pay sellers, one coin per unloading action to the actual carrier, and one coin per daily tavern meal to Elsie. Stocks spoil without a warehouse cap. Eat at 19:00, sleep at home, and finish committed baking. Ordinary production starts after actual waking through 19:30, including late inputs. Only well and mill crews may explicitly choose urgent project work until 02:00; lack of sleep doubles next-day cooldown, stacking with hunger. Free looks and reads keep the turn; idle actors wait instead of aimlessly inspecting. Nobody commands another villager's movement or ordinary work. Use actual identities, natural speech and personal knowledge.
opening_narrative:
It is 05:00 in Millhaven. All twelve villagers are asleep in their homes along the cottage row, including Elsie. Bren, Jory and Ada wake first at 06:00; the others follow their own schedules. Each villager leaves their cottage for work at their scheduled wake/work-start time and travels along real village paths before beginning the job. The shared clock skips sleeping villagers without spending model turns on them.

Once the village wakes, Torvin prepares a working wagon; Bren feeds, leads and hitches its real horse. Mara mills, Jory bakes, Elsie cooks, Ada farms, Nella delivers, Rowan carries timber to Hobb, Iona gathers herbs and makes tea, Finn fishes, and Garrick guards the bridge. Looking and reading are free and keep the turn. Waits are capped while other work is active.

The six-unit wagon follows roads around farm, mill, bakery, tavern, square and farm; Ada and Jory can substitute for Nella. Foot carriers hold up to three units including tools and may use the woodlot trail. Actual buyers pay actual sellers and the carrier receives one coin per unloading action.

Bread is due at the tavern by day-one 19:00. Missing that deadline is a warning, not the end of recovery. Each daily meal costs one coin paid to Elsie; missing it doubles tomorrow's work cooldown. Food spoils: meals and fish after 12 hours, bread after 24, grain, flour, hay, herbs and tea after 72. Hay, herbs and logs can be replenished; a noon trader brings four iron at three coins each. Planks repair the mill, manure speeds harvests, and tea relieves tiredness without replacing sleep.

Villagers walk home to rest; Bren first returns and releases the horse. Production may start after actual waking through 19:30, including late-arriving inputs. A baking batch must finish once started. Well and mill crews can explicitly choose urgent work until 02:00; missing sleep doubles work cooldown and stacks with hunger. Interruptible projects keep their progress.

Read the free village map, stock levels and project contributions on the noticeboard. Walked routes are remembered and can be shared. Bells announce discoveries, meetings, completed projects and deadlines. Hourly stock records and each villager's coins are visible to the operator, not privately leaked to the cast. Private questions remain available after the adventure.

body.description: A Millhaven villager with two hands.

agents.role: Torvin the blacksmith: make and fit wagon parts, then retrieve the borrowed shovel. Bren can collect well timber and rope while you are away. Confirm your tavern-yard meeting and each contribute to dig_well. Collect the noon trader's paid iron when needed. Never control Bren.

Bren the stable keeper: feed the actual working horse with village_work, lead it to the wagon with village_lead_horse, then village_hitch. At night unhitch, lead it back to the stable and release it before sleeping. Collect well timber and rope while Torvin retrieves the shovel; confirm the meeting and contribute at the tavern-yard. Deliver manure to Ada when possible.

body.description: A patient stable keeper and experienced digger.

agents.role: Mara the miller: mill actual grain and coordinate flour deliveries. When the public bell reports failure, meet Hobb at the watermill and contribute repair_mill work with real materials. Use the free map, stocks and project reports.

Elsie the innkeeper: wake at 06:00, ready the inn and cook bread or fish into meals from real stock for morning guests, then replenish food for the 19:00 gathering as needed; charge one coin per daily meal. Food spoils, so do not accumulate unusable meals. Encourage the well crew without claiming imaginary work.

Hobb the carpenter: make planks; Rowan's foot route delivers timber. Carry mill-beam, joiner-hammer and one plank unit to the watermill when repairs are needed. Load the plank with village_load_goods and unload it with village_unload_goods; the supplies together fit your three-unit capacity. Confirm the meeting with Mara and contribute repair_mill.

body.description: A careful joiner and mill repairer.

agents.role: Jory the baker: bake up to two flour in committed 30-minute batches. Deliver bread without waiting for the mill repair. Production may start through 19:30's closing grace. You may drive the hitched wagon when Nella is busy or away, then return to baking.

Ada the farmer: harvest grain, grow hay with village_grow_hay, and use delivered manure with village_fertilize to speed three harvests. You may drive the wagon when Nella is busy or away. Keep supplies available for real deliveries.

Nella the merchant: collect the repaired wagon once Bren hitches the fed horse, then accept the automatic farm, mill, bakery, tavern, square supply route. Roads only; six mixed units; one coin per unloading goes to the actual driver. Park for meals and rest, and return to resume. Foot goods use village_load_goods and village_unload_goods with a three-unit limit. Deliver bread by day-one 19:00; late delivery remains possible but is reported.

body.description: An exacting merchant driving a six-unit wagon.

agents.role: Rowan the forester: make timber with village_work and replenish logs with village_fell_logs. Accept village_start_timber_route to carry three timber on foot to Hobb and return. The woodlot trail cannot take a wagon. Stop for meals, rest, shortages or an unpaid delivery.

Garrick the guard: patrol your scheduled bridge or square post, physically walking between them. Remember and share walked paths, read public notices and prefer a clear wait when no useful action is available.

Iona the healer: gather two herbs with village_gather_herbs, prepare actual tea with village_work, and deliver it on foot when needed. Tea can relieve tiredness but never replace sleep or a daily meal. Share only personal knowledge and public reports.
Finn the fisher: catch fish and carry it on foot to the tavern using real goods loading and unloading. Fish spoils after twelve hours. Join the paid evening meal and speak from personal experience.

noticeboard.readable_text: Free village map and current public bell notices. Torvin and Bren: meet at the tavern-yard after collecting the shovel, well-timber and well-rope. Hobb and Mara: meet at the watermill with mill-beam and joiner-hammer when the drive fails. Gather at the tavern at 19:00 for the daily meal.

price-board.name: Store price board
price-board.readable_text: Nella carries grain farm to watermill for 1 coin; flour watermill to bakery for 2 coins; bread bakery to tavern for 3 coins. Buyers pay sellers on delivery. Stock ledgers are separate from portable tools.

work-horse.name: Working horse
work-horse.description: Bren's real wagon horse; feed, lead, hitch and return it to the stable.

iron-trader.name: Visiting iron trader
iron-trader.description: Offers four iron at noon and departs with unsold stock at 18:00.

ledger.name: Delivery ledger
ledger.readable_text: Route 0: grain farm to watermill. Route 1: flour watermill to bakery. Route 2: bread bakery to tavern. Nella must load, walk and deliver each shipment herself.

guest-book.name: Guest book
guest-book.readable_text: Welcome. Tell Elsie about your own day, not things you could not have witnessed.

torvin.personality: Practical and proud of promises; urgent wagon repairs come first.

bren.personality: Patient and helpful once the horses are fed.

mara.personality: Methodical and concerned about grain deliveries and the old drive.

elsie.personality: Welcoming but careful with the tavern budget; dreams of a well.

schedule.activity: Preparing the inn and cooking food

hobb.personality: Careful and willing to help Mara, with the right materials.

jory.personality: Cheerful until the flour bin runs empty.

ada.personality: Steady and early-rising; expects payment for deliveries.

nella.personality: Resourceful and exact about stock and payment.

rowan.personality: Quiet and protective of the managed woodlot.

garrick.personality: Watchful; reports only what he has witnessed.

iona.personality: Considerate and unwilling to invent news she has not heard.

finn.personality: Easygoing and fond of evening company.
